messages:
sasha: quick ask — can someone run a short hardware SKU comparison for our inference runtime? target model: ref-7B (FP16 path). Need p99 latency and tokens/sec for batch sizes [1,8,32] and seq lengths [512,2048]. please include A100(40GB), H100(80GB), L40S if available. want numbers + exact command used. thanks!

jeff: I can take this. I'll use the dedicated perf lab (gpu-pool-qa) and run the microbench harness. ETA a few hours. any specific perf flags (kv-cache warmup, disable bundling)?

sasha: keep defaults but enable kv-cache warmup for long sequences; disable model-parallel so it's single-GPU for apples-to-apples. include stable seed and 3 runs per config.

infra-bot: @jeff scheduled job perf-bench/1718501123 on gpu-pool-qa (A100,H100,L40S). will post logs to /mnt/perf/results/1718501123/

jeff: starting with A100 now. command I ran:

```bash
./bin/run_bench --model ref-7B --dtype fp16 --devices 1 \
  --batch-sizes 1,8,32 --seq-lens 512,2048 \
  --kv-warmup 2 --runs 3 --output ./results/1718501123/a100.csv
```

jeff: quick note — on A100 I saw OOM at bs=32, seq=2048 with default tensor shapes; I reduced internal workspace to avoid OOM and retried (this may affect throughput a bit). posting summary table below (p99 in ms, tokens/sec = sum tokens / wall):

```
A100-40GB
bs | seq | p99 (ms) | tps (tokens/sec)
1  | 512  | 42      | 48k
8  | 512  | 120     | 380k
32 | 512  | 460     | 1.1M
1  | 2048 | 170     | 12k
8  | 2048 | 560     | 85k
32 | 2048 | OOM*    | -
```

jeff: uploading full CSV + perf traces to S3: s3://redwood-perf/bench/1718501123/a100/

maria: thanks — could you also capture GPU metrics (SM utilization, power, mem bw) via nvidia-smi/dcgm at same time? helps explain perf delta.

jeff: yes, DCGM logs included in the folder.

jeff: moved to H100 now. same command, results:

```
H100-80GB
bs | seq | p99 (ms) | tps
1  | 512  | 28      | 72k
8  | 512  | 90      | 500k
32 | 512  | 330     | 1.5M
1  | 2048 | 120     | 17k
8  | 2048 | 380     | 120k
32 | 2048 | 1400    | 320k
```

jeff: H100 handled bs=32/2048 but latency increases (mem pressure). DCGM shows high sustained HBM bw ~650GB/s.

ryan: interesting — H100 gives ~2-3x better small-batch latency vs A100. can you also run with kernel fusion flags on (if runtime supports) to see latency improvements for bs=1?

jeff: good idea, I'll run one extra pass with --enable-fusion

infra-bot: job perf-bench/1718501123-fusion queued on H100

jeff: fusion run (H100):

```
H100-fusion
bs=1 seq=512 p99 22ms (was 28ms)
bs=1 seq=2048 p99 95ms (was 120ms)
```

jeff: now L40S run (single card availability limited). results:

```
L40S
bs | seq | p99 (ms) | tps
1  | 512  | 30      | 68k
8  | 512  | 110     | 450k
32 | 512  | 380     | 1.4M
1  | 2048 | 130     | 15k
8  | 2048 | 420     | 108k
32 | 2048 | 1000    | 450k
```

maria: L40S numbers look close to H100 at small batch but tails worse for large batch seq=2048. can you attach the full DCGM timelines and perf traces? also note whether SW stack used cuda 12 vs 11 (driver differences matter).

jeff: stack: CUDA 12.1, libcudnn 9.4, driver 535.xx for H100/L40S; A100 run used driver 515.xx (lab still has old nodes) — that's a variable. added note in results README.

sasha: excellent — this is exactly what we needed. next steps:
- infra: try to standardize driver versions across pools (jeff/infra)
- perf: add fusion-enabled baseline for public benchmarks (devx)
- product: pick default recommended SKU for low-latency (sasha)

devx: I'll draft a short PR to update docs with H100 as recommended for p99-sensitive apps and include an asterisk about driver parity and kv-warmup. also add the bench commands to the repo.

jeff: final note — attaching raw logs + traces path: /mnt/perf/results/1718501123/ plus s3://redwood-perf/bench/1718501123/

infra-bot: uploaded artifacts and DCGM files for all runs. :white_check_mark:

sasha: great work, thanks team :thumbsup: we'll follow up in the perf sync next week.
